transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SA), Dana Lewis (CISO, ZenithCorp), Ravi Patel (Lead ML Eng), Angela Moore (Privacy Counsel), Tom Erickson (IT Ops)

Summary:
Quick security and privacy review focused on data handling: retention of prompts/responses, PII/PHI handling, confirmation that customer data is not used to train models, KMS/encryption options (BYOK/CMK), audit logs & SSO/RBAC, and data residency for a pilot. Follow-ups to include SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS notes, and sample logs.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 Type II & ISO 27001 attestations
- RBAC and SSO (SAML/Okta) configuration
- Audit logs and retention / export
- Encryption at rest and in transit, KMS / BYOK / HSM options
- Data residency (US-only vs multi-region)
- Prompt/content retention and deletion policies; PII/PHI handling; training opt-out 

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we'll jump into the security and privacy parts, happy to hand over to Priya for the deep technicals.
[00:12] Dana (ZenithCorp - CISO): Hi, Dana here. We mainly want to confirm the data lifecycle and the no-training on customer data commitments, plus how audit logs look.
[00:20] Ethan: Absolutely, that's top of list. Priya?
[00:23] Priya (Redwood SE): Hey all, good to meet you. I'll start with an overview — then we can dive into specifics. I'll call out where default Hosted behavior differs from Dedicated and Private deployments.
[00:35] Priya: So, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 are available — we'll send the attestations after the call — those live in our security pack. For RBAC/SSO we support SAML 2.0, Okta, Azure AD, and can map roles to groups for least privilege.
[00:50] Ravi (ZenithCorp): Great. For audit logs, we need immutable, time-stamped logs of every API call, who initiated it, and the prompt/response payloads — is that available?
[01:05] Priya: Yes. By default we capture request metadata, timestamps, user ID, model used, latency, and optionally full payloads. For Hosted customers, payload retention is configurable — default is 30 days for debugging. You can opt into a shorter retention or disable payload storage; metadata/audit logs remain for longer.
[01:25] Angela (ZenithCorp - Privacy Counsel): "Disable payload storage" — does that mean zero bytes of content are stored, or is there an obfuscated copy? We're concerned about PII/PHI in prompts.
[01:38] Priya: For Hosted we offer three modes: 1) full retention (debugging) 2) no payloads retained (only metadata/audit) 3) redaction mode where we attempt to detect and redact PII before persisting. Redaction isn't perfect so for regulated PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private where logs can stay in your VPC.
[01:58] Dana: Important for us: we need a legal attestation that Redwood does not use customer prompts/responses to train models or improve the underlying model weights. Can you say that on record?
[02:12] Ethan: Yes — public policy and contractual language: Redwood does not train or fine-tune our model fleet on customer-provided prompts or responses. Data used for improving models is on opt-in basis only and is scrubbed/aggregated; enterprise customers can opt-out by default. We'll attach the contractual clause in the security pack.
[02:33] Tom (IT Ops): For Dedicated, is customer data stored on our dedicated GPU hosts only and isolated from other tenants?
[02:42] Priya: Correct. Dedicated is tenant-isolated compute and storage. For Private deployments, everything is in your VPC/on-prem and Redwood control plane can be customer-managed for added isolation.
[02:55] Ravi: On encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and BYOK? We have strict key rotation and KMS policies.
[03:05] Priya: Yes. Hosted supports envelope encryption with options for Redwood-managed keys or BYOK via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault. We also support HSM-backed keys for FIPS requirements. For Private you can supply keys that never leave your environment. We'll provide integration notes.
[03:23] Dana: How about auditability — can we export logs to our SIEM and get a structured schema?
[03:31] Priya: We provide export connectors and can stream logs to your S3, Cloud Storage, or SIEM in JSON format. We'll share sample schema and a sample export.
[03:41] Angela: What about deletion requests for individual prompts? Suppose a user requests deletion under privacy law — can you delete specific records?
[03:51] Priya: Yes, we support targeted deletion. In Hosted mode we can delete payloads and mark them purged; metadata may remain for telemetry. In Dedicated/Private you have full control and can run deletion jobs yourself. We'll include the endpoint and the SLA for deletion in the docs.
[04:08] Ravi: Any chance the transcriptions or logs contain model internal states like KV cache or anything sensitive?
[04:16] Priya: No, we don't persist KV cache or internal model state in logs. Logs are limited to request/response payloads, metadata, and system-level events.
[04:24] Ethan: I want to emphasize two points: 1) No training on customer data by default, contractual confirmation coming. 2) On Hosted, payload retention is configurable and can be disabled; for PHI we recommend Dedicated/Private.
[04:36] Dana: Good. Let's talk about data residency — our data must remain in US regions only. Is that configurable?
[04:44] Priya: Yes, you can restrict routing to US-only regions and we can pin Dedicated capacity in specific regions. For Hosted, we have regional routing policies and can set a US-only policy for your org. We'll document the controls.
[04:57] Tom: How about incident response and notification SLAs? If there's a breach or suspected data exposure, what's timeline and evidence?
[05:05] Ethan: Our incident response process is in the security pack — standard is notify within 72 hours for confirmed breaches; we provide a preliminary report, scope, and remediation. We can discuss enterprise SLAs for faster notifications as part of contract.
[05:18] Angela: Can you describe how RBAC is structured? We need fine-grained roles so engineers can't access billing or audit logs.
[05:26] Priya: Roles map to permissions — admin, developer, auditor, billing. We support scoping at org, team, and project levels. Audit logs record who changed roles. SSO via SAML/Okta maps groups to roles.
[05:37] Ravi: For the pilot we may want to run redaction + short retention and stream logs to our SIEM. Will that impact latency?
[05:46] Priya: Minimal. Redaction happens asynchronously for most flows; it might add a small overhead (~10-30ms) to request processing depending on payload size. Batching/throughput settings can be tuned.
[05:58] Ethan: There's also a compliance question about subprocessor list — do you maintain a list of cloud providers and third-party subprocessors?
[06:05] Priya: Yes we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor list and BAAs where required. We'll include that in the pack.
[06:12] Dana: Are audit logs tamper-evident? Can we get signed log digests or S3 Object Lock?
[06:20] Priya: We can support S3 Object Lock for write-once-read-many, and we can provide signed digests for exports; we also have options to stream logs to your SIEM so you control retention immutability.
[06:31] Ravi: One last technical Q: do you ever use customer data to tune model prompts or system prompts that could leak between orgs?
[06:40] Priya: No cross-org leakage. System prompts and model configs used by the runtime are not derived from customer-specific content. Any tuning is either Redwood-internal on synthetic/opt-in datasets or isolated to private instances if you opt for that.
[06:54] Angela: We'll need explicit contract language and the standard security addendum with opt-out for data usage.
[07:01] Ethan: We'll include the clause and highlight it in the pack.
[07:05] -- brief pause while Ethan shares link to security pack --
[07:20] Ethan: I've dropped links in chat: security pack, SOC2 attestation, ISO cert, and sample log schema.
[07:27] Dana: Thanks. Seeing the sample schema helps. Can you also share an example of redaction behavior on a prompt with PHI?
[07:35] Priya: We'll share a small redaction demo and the false-positive/false-negative rates — redaction is pattern-based plus ML heuristics. For strict PHI compliance, Dedicated/Private is the recommendation.
[07:52] Ravi: Any performance differences if we disable payload logging?
[07:57] Priya: No measurable difference; logging is asynchronous. Batching, KV cache, and GPU sizing have larger impact.
[08:06] Dana: For the record, we need to know retention defaults: metadata 365 days, payloads 30 days by default, but configurable. Can you confirm?
[08:15] Priya: Yes, default Hosted settings: payloads 30 days, metadata 365. We can shorten both. Dedicated/Private defaults are set by customer.
[08:25] Tom: Is there an API we can call to purge data for a specific end-user?
[08:30] Priya: Yes, a delete endpoint that accepts identifiers and returns a purge token. We'll include the API docs.
[08:37] Ethan: Okay, let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[08:40] Ethan: Action items — we'll send the security pack and SOC/ISO certs; Priya will provide KMS notes and sample logs; Zenith to confirm residency and PII scope. Plan to follow up week of Dec 20 to start pilot.
[08:54] Dana: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:57] Ravi: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[09:00] Ethan: Thanks, we'll follow up via email with the attachments.
